What we do

Spaces where young people can actually breathe, grow and belong.

Six programmes, one promise: every child, woman and young person is heard, protected, mentored, educated and supported to grow.

01

Mentorship & personal development

One-to-one guidance and group mentorship that builds confidence, identity and life direction.

  • Monthly mentor circles
  • Goal-setting
  • Confidence workshops
02

SRHR & life skills

Age-appropriate education on health, consent, relationships and informed decision-making.

  • Puberty & health talks
  • Consent education
  • Safe-choices sessions
03

Community engagement & empowerment

Working with families, schools and community leaders to create supportive ecosystems.

  • Parent forums
  • School partnerships
  • Leader dialogues
04

Education & scholarships

Keeping girls and boys in school through materials, tuition support and advocacy.

  • School kits
  • Tuition support
  • Retention follow-up
05

GBV prevention & child protection

Teaching boundaries, safe reporting and building protection systems that truly work.

  • Safeguarding training
  • Reporting pathways
  • Safe-space clubs
06

Support for girls and boys

Inclusive spaces where every young person is seen, heard and equipped to thrive.

  • Peer clubs
  • Leadership training
  • Career exposure

About us

Our story

“Our founder grew up believing mentorship was a privilege, not something every young person could count on. NAKAJAH exists so that stops being true.”

What began as a handful of after-school conversations has grown into a movement of mentors, educators and advocates working together so that no child grows up guessing.

Mentorship
Protection
Empowerment

Safe spaces first. Every programme is built around psychological safety, confidentiality and youth voice, because growth only happens when you feel safe enough to ask questions.

Our Mission

To create safe and nurturing spaces where children, women and young people are heard, protected, mentored, educated and empowered with the knowledge, opportunities and confidence to thrive and transform their lives and communities.

Through mentorship, advocacy, education, protection and sustainable empowerment, we work to prevent violence, promote equality and ensure no one is left behind because of their circumstances.

ProtectedEmpoweredEquippedInspired
How it works

The NAKAJAH journey

Five steps that take a young person from feeling unseen to leading others.

1

Listen

We start by listening to young people, parents and teachers, so every programme answers a real need.

2

Protect

Safe spaces, clear boundaries and trusted reporting channels come before anything else.

3

Mentor

Each young person is matched with a trusted adult who walks with them, month after month.

4

Equip

Leadership, money skills, health knowledge and education support turn confidence into capability.

5

Launch

Graduates move into school, work and service, and become mentors for the next cohort.

The NAKAJAH way

Values that grow with you.

NAKAJAH is an acronym we live by. Each letter is a promise we make to every child, girl and young person who walks through our doors.

N

Nurture Identity

Through story circles, affirmation work and creative expression, every child learns who they are before the world tells them who to be.

Meet the founder

Dr. Lilian Odinakachi Onyeizu, PhD

Gender & Development Consultant · Author · Mentor

She leads NAKAJAH Care Foundation from a deeply held conviction that no child, woman, or young person should have their future limited by a lack of knowledge, guidance, protection, or opportunity.

Driven by the belief that the right support, safe spaces and meaningful mentorship can change the direction of a life, she founded NAKAJAH to help people discover their worth, find their voice, make informed decisions and become active participants in transforming their own lives and communities.

For Dr. Lilian, NAKAJAH is more than an organisation; it is a commitment to making hope accessible and ensuring that every individual has the opportunity to thrive.
